overrides.why: Anterior touch neurons: classic circuit hypothesis (Chalfie et al. 1985; consistent with Wicks & Rankin 1996) is gap junctions onto same-direction (reverse) command interneurons and inhibitory chemical synapses onto opposite-direction (forward) ones. Receptor dominance cannot see synapse-specific receptor localisation.

Posterior touch: same hypothesis mirrored (inhibit opposite-direction reverse interneurons). LUA is included as the PLM->PVC relay of the posterior touch pathway (Chalfie et al. 1985); treating its synapses onto reverse interneurons as inhibitory is OUR EXTENSION of that hypothesis.

Forward/reverse command modules are antagonistic: AVA and AVB activity is anticorrelated in whole-brain imaging (Kato et al. 2015), and fitting polarities to ablation data gives mostly inhibitory locomotor-interneuron synapses (Rakowski et al. 2013).
